about.title: The Bridge Between British and Libyan Business
about.p1: The Libyan British Business council (LBBC) was established in 2004 to promote trade and investment between the UK and Libya. We provide a unique platform for our members to network, share insights, and develop strategic partnerships in one of the world's most promising emerging markets.
about.missionText: To be the primary facilitator of trade and investment between the UK and Libya, fostering sustainable economic growth and mutual prosperity.
about.leadershipText: Led by experienced professionals with deep expertise in international trade, diplomacy, and the Libyan market.
about.leadershipBioFallback: {name} is a key member of the LBBC leadership team, bringing extensive experience in bilateral trade and international relations. As {role}, they play a vital role in shaping the council's strategic direction and supporting our members in navigating the UK-Libya commercial landscape.

page.title: Advancing UK-Libya Bilateral Trade Since 2004
page.overviewP1: Established in 2004, the Libyan British Business Council (LBBC) is a non-political association dedicated to promoting trade and investment between the United Kingdom and Libya. As a trade promotion body, we act as a practical resource for our members, helping companies across all major sectors navigate the complexities of bilateral commerce.
page.overviewP2: Our membership comprises a wide range of leading UK and Libyan companies. This collective network provides a platform for shared expertise and reliable partnerships, ensuring our members have the support they need to work effectively in both markets.
page.overviewP3: Operating with strict neutrality, the LBBC remains focused on fostering sustainable economic ties. We provide the networking opportunities, market insights, and advocacy required to help our members turn business potential into successful, long-term operations.
page.feature1Text: Dedicated solely to commercial and economic partnership.
page.feature2Text: Strengthening ties between the UK and Libyan markets.
page.feature3Text: Access to insights from experts across energy, finance and more.
page.missionDesc: To facilitate and promote business relations between the UK and Libya by providing a neutral, professional platform for connectivity, market insight, and commercial growth.
page.pillar1Text: We create opportunities for UK and Libyan businesses to build meaningful relationships. From trade delegations and face-to-face meetings to high-profile receptions in London and Libya, we provide the platforms where partnerships are formed.
page.pillar2Text: Staying informed is critical to navigating any market. We provide our members with real-time economic updates, monthly webinars featuring key experts, and high-quality business reports that offer a clear view of current business developments.
page.pillar3Text: We act as a dedicated voice for our members’ interests. By working closely with our partners, government departments, and economic stakeholders in both countries, we offer the advocacy, travel support, and business guidance necessary to operate.

fullStory.title: LBBC Member Spotlight: Capterio
fullStory.p1: This week, the LBBC spotlight is on our member Capterio, which has played a central role in the conversation on how Libya can turn gas flaring from waste into value.
fullStory.p2: As part of the UK–Libya Roundtable hosted by the LBBC at Libya Energy & Economic Summit 2026, Capterio’s CEO, Mark Jonathan Davis, joined Libyan and international stakeholders in Tripoli to explore practical pathways to capture and monetise flared gas in support of Libya’s economic goals.
fullStory.p3: Capterio is a UK-based flared solutions company that is focused on monetising waste gas. Using its satellite-based near real-time flare tracking technology, the company works with operators, governments and financiers to quantify flaring for every asset every day, helping to improve visibility, drive operational improvements and identify and prioritise flare capture projects.
fullStory.p4: In Libya, Capterio’s analysis shows that capturing around 7 BCM of currently flared gas each year could unlock an estimated US$2–3 billion in additional national revenues, strengthen domestic energy security and reduce emissions using technologies already available today.
fullStory.p5: Capterio’s participation at the Summit and Roundtable illustrates how specialist international expertise can support Libya’s ambitions to reduce flaring and monetise its gas resources more effectively.
fullStory.p6: Join the LBBC member network for access to exclusive networking events and insights from webinars, briefings and newsletters, and to help shape the next phase of UK–Libya trade.
fullStory.cta: Learn more about becoming an LBBC member here.

membership.title: Why Join? Your Edge in Bilateral Trade
membership.desc: Joining the LBBC integrates your business into a trusted bilateral ecosystem. Because operating across the UK and Libya requires reliable information and secure partnerships, we provide the dedicated platforms to help you stay informed and connected. By becoming a member, you gain an operational advantage built on four key pillars:
membership.pillar1Desc: Secure unique networking opportunities through our targeted events. We deliver meaningful introductions to visiting Libyan business leaders, key decision-makers, government officials, and potential joint-venture partners.
membership.pillar2Desc: Make informed, strategic decisions using our high-level market intelligence. Members stay ahead of the curve with exclusive business briefings, monthly sector reports, and ongoing market updates.
membership.pillar3Desc: Navigate the bureaucratic realities of international trade with practical support. We provide actionable advice on meeting regulatory requirements, overcoming red tape, and securing fast-tracked business visas.
membership.pillar4Desc: Participate in a reciprocal referral network designed to connect our members to your specialized services, and refer you to the guidance of our network's experts when you face specific trade and investment challenges.
membership.cta: Become a part of the premiere network for UK-Libya trade.

membership.governanceTitle: Upholding the Highest Standards of Commercial Integrity
membership.governanceDesc: The LBBC is committed to fostering a business environment built on transparency, ethical conduct, and strict adherence to international regulatory frameworks. Our governance policies ensure that all members and partners operate with the integrity required to maintain the credibility of the UK-Libya commercial corridor.

governancePolicies.title: Anti-Bribery & Corruption (ABC) Policy
governancePolicies.content: The LBBC operates with a strict zero-tolerance approach to bribery and corruption. We are committed to acting professionally, fairly, and with integrity in all our business dealings, network facilitations, and partnerships. The Council strictly adheres to the provisions of the UK Bribery Act 2010 and equivalent international legislation. We require all members, board directors, and staff to uphold these highest ethical standards, ensuring transparent and lawful conduct across all UK and Libyan operations.

governancePolicies.title: Sanctions Compliance
governancePolicies.content: Navigating international trade requires rigorous regulatory awareness. The LBBC strictly monitors and adheres to all applicable international sanctions regimes, including those mandated by the United Nations (UN) and the UK Government’s Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) concerning Libya. We conduct standard due diligence and will not facilitate trade, provide introductions, or offer support services to any individual, entity, or subsidiary subject to international sanctions.

governancePolicies.title: Member Code of Conduct
governancePolicies.content: Membership within the LBBC carries a responsibility to uphold the credibility of the bilateral business community. All members are expected to conduct their commercial activities with professionalism, transparency, and ethical integrity. Furthermore, members must respect the LBBC’s strictly non-partisan and neutral stance regarding internal political affairs in both the UK and Libya. The Board of Directors reserves the right to suspend or terminate the membership of any organisation found to be in breach of these standards, involved in unlawful practices, or acting in a manner detrimental to the Council’s mandate.

governancePolicies.title: Data Protection & Privacy
governancePolicies.content: The LBBC is deeply committed to protecting the privacy and security of our members' commercial data and personal information. We operate in full compliance with the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and the Data Protection Act 2018. Any information shared with the Secretariat is handled with strict confidentiality, utilised solely for the purpose of delivering membership services, and is never sold or distributed to unauthorized third parties.

questions.q: Does my company need to be registered in the UK or Libya to join?
questions.a:
No, your company does not need to be registered in the UK or Libya to become a member.

However, prospective members must have a genuine commercial interest in the bilateral corridor and a demonstrable presence in either country — such as a registered office, branch, or active business operations.

The LBBC welcomes applications from organisations based anywhere in the world, provided they meet these criteria.

questions.q: What types of sectors and industries are currently represented in the LBBC network?
questions.a:
The LBBC network encompasses and supports a broad range of sectors and industries. Our network includes everything from specialized SMEs and independent consultants to multinational corporations.

While we welcome engagement from businesses across all commercial fields, our support is currently most active in the following key sectors: Energy, Power, Infrastructure, Financial & Professional Services, Logistics & Transport, Healthcare, Agriculture, and Education & Training.

While these represent our current engagement, our network is continually evolving. We welcome enquiries from organisations actively contributing to, or seeking to enter, the UK-Libya market.

questions.q: Is membership limited to commercial businesses or can NGOs and academic institutions join?
questions.a:
No, LBBC membership is not exclusively limited to commercial enterprises. We recognise the role that non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and academic institutions play within the UK-Libya ecosystem, particularly in areas of capacity building, research and bilateral cooperation.

To support their participation and engagement with the business community, the LBBC offers specially discounted membership rates for qualifying non-profits and academic institutions.

For more information regarding these discounted rates or to submit an enquiry about your organisation’s eligibility, please contact our team at events@lbbc.org.uk.

questions.q: What is the step-by-step process for submitting a membership application?
questions.a:
Applying for LBBC membership is a straightforward, three-step process:

1. Submit Your Application: Choose your membership tier and click the "Join Now" button above. You will be prompted to provide your organisation’s details, followed by the contact information for the primary individual representative.

2. Review and Invoicing: Our team will review your application. Upon approval, you will receive an email containing a secure payment link to remit the fee for your selected membership tier.

3. Onboarding and Access: Once payment is successfully processed, you will be officially welcomed into the LBBC network. You will be prompted to set up your member account, granting you access to explore the community network and register for upcoming events.

questions.q: How long does the membership review and approval process take?
questions.a: The membership review and approval process typically takes 2 to 3 business days. Upon submitting your application, our team will review your organisation's details promptly and contact you directly with the outcome and the next steps for completing your registration.

questions.q: If my application is currently under review, can I still register for upcoming LBBC events?
questions.a:
No, member-level event registration is only accessible once your application has been fully approved and your account onboarding is complete.

However, we understand that timing can be critical. If there is an upcoming event you wish to attend in the interim as a non-member, please contact our team at events@lbbc.org.uk. We will review your request and explore available options to facilitate your attendance.

questions.q: What currencies and payment methods are accepted for membership fees?
questions.a:
The LBBC accepts payment via bank transfer, international bank transfer, or through a secure payment link sent to your designated billing contact email. Visa and Mastercard are accepted.

Please note that due to current banking restrictions, payments cannot be processed directly from Libya. However, Libyan members are warmly welcomed and can complete their membership payment using an overseas bank account or internationally issued card.

questions.q: How are membership fees calculated and when are they due for renewal?
questions.a:
Membership fees are calculated based on your selected tier (Council, Corporate, or Sole Trader) and are valid for a period of 12 months from the date of your successful onboarding.

Renewal notifications will be sent to your primary contact 30 days prior to the expiration of your current term, providing you with a link to renew your membership and maintain uninterrupted access to the LBBC network and services.
